Messages.Author: Steve Bucy
Messages.Body:
I just read the Duelist #14 articles on the Sabbat. I am for one am not
very impressed. Besides the concerns about escalation and broken cards,
there are other things that bug.

1.) Major cross over disciplines on many of the new vampires. Ventrue
with aus, Gangrel with dom, etc. Pretty soon you will be able to use
almost any skill with any clan.

2.) Reprints of lots (not a couple), but lots of cards you just don't
need 20 more of. Couldn't they come up with similar but different cards.
Why do I have to waste money on more Cats Guidance, Regaining the Upper
Hand, etc..

3.) The disciplines are becoming more alike. Pretty soon every discipline
is going to have a S:CE.

I may be wrong but it is starting to seem like a money making racket.

Steve Bucy

P.S. For all you Tremere conspiracy believers: Have you noticed the
articles in the Duelist all end with the Thamaturgy symbol. Hmmmm...

And you also need a rulebook. Sabbat includes no rulebook, so is therefore
*not* a stand-alone product (WotC propaganda notwithstanding). If you
have to have VtES (or Jyhad) starters, then you don't need any more of
these commons. If you're forced to by other starters in order to play
with just the Sabbat cards, are you really going to not play with the
cards that came with your rulebook-bearing starter? No, unless paying
US$8.95 for a rulebook appeals to you.

(Granted, with net access, you do have access to some on-line sources
that may offer the rules in various forms, but then you're merely
replacing the Sabbat's dependence on VtES starters with a dependence
on net access).

Screwy marketing drones. Bah.

I disagree. It has always been possible(through use of skill cards)
to get vampires (well, at least one) that have any mix of disciplines
you want. The main consideration was the ease with which it could be
done. With trouble, you could make a (not necessarily effective) deck
that used any combination of disciplines. While some combinations are
more effective than others, there is simply no way to combine
disciplines in such a way that the game is really broken. Most
combos, no matter how effective, add more to the game (in terms of
variety and interest) than the detract (ie, make someone win all the
time). Obf. and Dom. makes one of the most effective combinations in
the game, and malkavians have both of these as clan disciplines. Obf.
and Pres. are complete opposites(the idea behind the powers, not what
the cards do) but they are amazingly effective when combined in a vote
deck, as setites(who have both disciplines as clan discipolines) can
easily do.
If you can't break the game with discipline combinations, then I, for
one, am all for making them easy to do. Each new deck adds something
to the game. One of the joys of playing a ccg is seeing new decks
that use new combinations of old cards. Why should interecept decks
be limited to a few clans? If someone wants to play a ventrue
interecept deck, I say let 'em. There's nothing wrong with it. Its
just different. I see that as a good thing. Similarly, a i'd rather
play with a new and interesting gangrel s&b deck than another combat
deck that uses essentially the same cards as all the others. (You
scorpion sting me with claws of the dead for 3 aggravated and prevent
all my damage? How innovative and clever!) Protean has always had
some great avoid combat/stealth cards, but only the gangrel had
protean, and the gangrel never did much but fight, so these cards were
rarely used. Encouraging the gangrel to move away from combat
essentially "un-obsoletes" these cards.
Clans with greater access to a wide variety of disciplines can be used
to make a wider variety of decks, making the game more interesting. I
see nothing wrong with not being able to figure out the entirety of
someone's library as soon as you see the first vampire.

> >> 2.) Reprints of lots (not a couple), but lots of cards you just don't
> >> need 20 more of. Couldn't they come up with similar but different cards.
> >> Why do I have to waste money on more Cats Guidance, Regaining the Upper
> >> Hand, etc..

Here, i agree with you. It would have been a simple thing for WOTC to
print cards that had abilities similar to those of cards already in
existance(thereby preserving the "flavor" of the disciplines) but that
were different enough that people would use them. A lot of other
disciplines could have benefited (as in been made more interesting,
not unreasonably more powerful) from gaining the kind of redundancy
that obfuscate, potence, and a few others have. I would certainly
have welcomed another animalism intercept card; you can only play one
cats per action, so you have to be packing a lot of raven spies to get
respectable intercept. With such limited options, few use animalism
intercept, so the cards are effectiveley wasted.
Oh, well. WOTC could have done something bettter than they did. What
else is new?

> >> 3.) The disciplines are becoming more alike. Pretty soon every discipline
> >> is going to have a S:CE.
> >
> >This is one thing I agree with. Part of deck construction was finding
> >disciplines that were compatable. Now ppl will be getting closer to one
> >discipline decks that neeed no other back up
> >
> Exactly.
>

I agree that if all the disciplines end up identical, or if one
discipline ends up able to do everything, that would be bad, but i
don't agree that givng disciplines powers that they didn't previously
have is necessarily bad. The example given, the branching out of
S:CE, is one case where it can be good. Most really good combat decks
will burn a vampire per combat if their opponent doesn't make a good
show of defending himself. Also, most combat decks have at least one
or two effective ways of dealing with s:CE. In a non-combat deck S:CE
is often necessary but not sufficient for survival. Time was, every
non-combat deck needed either presence or fortitude. The ventrue have
both of these, and all of the other clans that had one, specifically
the gangrel, the toreador, and the brujah, were quite often combat
decks. I see nothing wrong with the Malkavians beeing able to defend
themselves from rush combat.(Well, they can use Thoughts Betrayed,
but TB simply shouldn't exist. See my arguments on that thread.)

Messages.Author: Steve Bucy
Messages.Body:


I was not saying that cross over disciplines where "broken". Although I
they could change game balance. It is true that it has always been
possible to use any discipline with any clan due to skill cards. Skill
cards by nature however reduce the effectiveness of a deck. You can't
depend on getting the skill card you need unless you put in a lot of
them. If you put in lots of skill cards (at least 6 to be sure you get
one) you will hurt the effectiveness of the deck. This was a natural
limit on adding skills. This is no longer a consideration.
The real problem with crossover skills in my opinion is that they take
away originality. You used to have to think and be creative to make a
Gangrel Dominate S&B deck. With the Sabbat anyone can do it. Crossover
skills also destroy the uniqueness of each clan. The Ventrue where known
for their lack of intercept, which set them apart from the Toreador. With
the Sabbat they become almost like the Toreador. Each clan used to have
it's own strong and week points. With the Sabbat the clans are all
growing closer together. If this continues the clans will have no real
identity at all.

Steve Bucy

Messages.Author: Nathan Harada
Messages.Body:
> Steve Bucy wrote:
>
> I just read the Duelist #14 articles on the Sabbat. I am for one am not

> there are other things that bug.

> 1.) Major cross over disciplines on many of the new vampires. Ventrue
> with aus, Gangrel with dom, etc. Pretty soon you will be able to use
> almost any skill with any clan.

Ventrue antitribu are supposed to have Aus Dom For. I don't
understand how the Gangrel got Dom, but there are supposed to be
City (Cel Obf Pro) and Country (Reg.) In general, the Sabbat tend
to have more crossovers between disciplines than the Camarilla,
because they share blood and teach disciplines among themselves
frequently.
I like crossover vampires, with some of their clan powers
and another discipline. Kallista, Bear Paw, Justine...If certain
vampires allow certain strange combinations of disciplines, then
the game world is widened,and the better for it.
I don't like vampires taken so far that they have one clan
discipline and 3 non-clan. There is a Gangrel in Sabbat, a 3 cap.
with ani for. Protean is what makes the clan work, dammit. I
really hated Kalinda in AH-having no signature clan discipline at
6 was really too much.

> 2.) Reprints of lots (not a couple), but lots of cards you just don't
> need 20 more of. Couldn't they come up with similar but different cards.
> Why do I have to waste money on more Cats Guidance, Regaining the Upper
> Hand, etc..

Personally, I'd love to have more Cat's Guidances. They could
have done away with Regaining the Upper Hand, but most of the things
still in Sabbat are the basic, all-purpose things, like Undead Strength.
Wake's been changed.

> 3.) The disciplines are becoming more alike. Pretty soon every discipline
> is going to have a S:CE.

Obfuscate, IMO, should have had an S:Ce from the beginning.
Vanish from Mime's Eye should have been a S:Ce instead of Press to End,
Press. Auspex, however, should never have an S:Ce, and neither should
Celerity or Potence.

> I may be wrong but it is starting to seem like a money making racket.

Well. Here we are...WotC wants to make money. The real
reason we don't have as much *stuff* (NetRep, Duelist coverage, free
cards, $100 000 tournaments, etc) is that WotC doesn't pull as much
of a profit off of the small number of obsessives here as the
large number of obsessives in the other game.
But WotC doesn't want to intentionally lose _these_
obsessives, and followed their current trend of overpowering to
attract weenies with Ancient Hearts. Sabbat looks like more of
the same. Intention or not, overpowered cards are unpleasant,
in a game noted for balance.

> P.S. For all you Tremere conspiracy believers: Have you noticed the

> articles in the Duelist all end with the Thaumaturgy symbol. Hmmmm...

No, I did not. Eeeeeewww.
That might explain their special emphasis on Shotgun Ritual
and their inclusion of Ian Forestal in the previous Duelist.
OR maybe it's just a carry-over from the previous 40 Magic
articles, and they envision the Tremere methuselah as the opponent
in duels.

-Nathan Harada
At work building a Salubri expansion.

This can be a concern, especially if disciplines are doing things they

other hand, it might be nice to see some expansion in what can be done
with a specific discipline. Is there any reason why any discipline
SHOULDN'T have a S:CE (except maybe Potence, but even that may be justified)?

Wait just a moment here. Even though I will admit to believing that making
all of the clans alike is a bad thing, I don't think that that's exactly
the case of what's happening here(or even if it is, that we can be sure
about that yet).

Obfuscate is getting an S:CE. IMHO, It should have had it from the beginning.

Celerity is getting bleed; nice, but it's probably going to be really
expensive and restricted(like cat burglary). If it's not, then I'll
worry and complain with the rest of you.

Thaumaturgy is getting first round aggs(gulp) via shotgun ritual. This
_is_ a bad thing(TM). But not because it makes the clans alike; because
it gives the tremere an ability which they, as far as I can tell, do not
need, and have never needed.

The cross over of disciplines is a good thing; it encourages diversity
in deck construction, which adds to the game. I like the idea of some
sick person out there making an effective Ventrue combat deck; maybe
It'll become possible. Maybe not. But even the cross-over in Sabbat
(With the exception of Ian Forestal) won't make it as mindless as you
might think; some of the gangrel w/ dominate don't have protean at all.

The ability to have a clan do something other than what it normally does
adds an interesting aspect to the game; but without work and some skill
in deck building, it will be difficult to make the clan as effective in
the non-specialized area as in the specialized one. And such divergences,
in my experience, have been fragile and easily disrupted(My malkies w/
flamethrowers deck is a good example; it dies when anyone pulls a Rotshreck).
That the possibility exists is good. Making it mindless(which I don't think
Sabbat will do; I can't see my Obfuscate/Protean/Dominate deck being too easy
to make even w/ Sabbat) is bad.

Of course, if Sabbat does make it mindless I'll be just as ticked as you are.
But right now, I don't see that it will. We'll just have to wait
and see the set to reach any conclusions.

Alec Chang

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
James Hamblin wrote:
"The thing that gets my goat about this is that their attitude is "Now the
Tremere don't have to wait until the second round", as if that were a good
thing. Hee, hee. Now I can get burned on the first round. Yay!"

I really fail to see how Shorgun Ritual will really help out the Tremere
all that much. Barring the use of Thoughts Betrayed (which is well
regarded as a broken and/or inappropriate card for the game), the
Tremere's big problem is not that all of their good strikes are second
round, it is that they have no way to avoid getting messed up in the first
place and/or making ANY of their strikes useful at all, be them first or
second round.

The Tremere cannot deal with S:CE, Dodge/Aditional Strike, Immortal
Grapple, or anything else that nullifies their strikes. Regardless of
whether or not the Tremere can use their cool second round strikes on the
first round, if they are Immortally Grappled, they can't do anything. If
their opponent plays a S:CE, they can't do anything. If their opponent
has dodges and aditional strikes, they can't do anything. In any of
these situations, having the ability to play Walk of Flame the first round
will have no bearing on the combat. It will just cost the Tremere 2 extra
blood, causing them to die even faster.

The main problem with the Tremere in combat always has been (again,
ignoring Thoughts Betrayed) that against a non combat ready deck, they
will kill them outright, regardless of the fact that their good strikes
are 2nd round only, but against a good combat deck they will just be
killed as they do not have Celerity or Fortitude to fall back on to help
them be useful in the first round (I'm sure that someone somewhere has
made a good Tremere THA/CEL deck or something, but I am sticking to their
basic disciplines)

Basically, Shotgun Ritual will not measurably help out the Tremere in any
way that matters. If used against a non combat deck (that does not
imedately S:CE or Dodge all of your strikes, mind you), you are paying 2
blood to avoid pressing, which they probably can't prevent anyway. Hardly
seems worth it. If used against a good combat deck, the Tremere will pay
2 blood to be able to play 2nd round cards imediately, but that will be
completely in vain as you will be Immortally Grappled or your opponent
will dodge your strike and then beat you senseless with Blur or something.
All Shotgun Ritual will really do is make fights where the Tremere were
going to win a bit quicker while making fights that the Tremere was going
to lose, well, a bit quicker.

If we choose to not ignore Thoughts Betrayed, Shotgun Ritual is also
useless, as why use Shotgun Ritual in your deck and still get Immortally
Grappled or S:CE'ed, when you can just play TB and simply press into the
next round and kill your opponent anyway?

Granted, all of this is based on the assumption that Shotgun Ritual is a
card that says something like "Second round only Tha strikes may be played
on the first round", as everyone seems to be under the impression of. If
it allows Blood to Water on the first round, then, well, I'll just cover
my head...

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
rj...@uswest.com (Randy J. Ray) writes:
>Unless I'm mistaken, dodges do not prevent blood loss from stolen blood?

Dodges prevent all effects of the opposing strike[1]. This includes
damage, stealing blood, paralyzation[2], stealing/destroying equipment,
and losing skill cards.

The only thing Dodge cannot cancel is a Strike: Combat Ends.

Notes:
[1]: It actually only voids the opposing strike's effects on the Dodging
minion and his equipment (not his retainers, nor any side effects
that the strike has one the striking minion).
[2]: Jyhad - there is no paralyzation in VtES.

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Nathan Harada wrote:

"Possible. But how many decks can really kill a largish
Tremere first round?"

My main point about Shotgun Ritual as a concept was that if the Tremere
are fighting someone who is going to kill them, playing second round
strikes on the first round will not measurably help them. If they are
fighting a good combat deck, then being able to Cauldron of Blood or Walk
of Flame someone on the first round will not really help them, as they
will still get Immortally Grappled or Acrobatics'ed, or Fortituded (vs.
Cauldron or Flame...). If, on the other hand, the Tremere are fighting a
deck that cannot match them in combat, being able to play second round
strikes on the first round won't make any difference, as they would
probably be able to press into the second round anyway (except aginst
S:CE, where again, Shotgun won't help)

I'm sure that there are some situations (like the ones you pointed out,
the Fast Reaction combo springs to mind as a good one that I had not
thought of intially) where Shotgun Ritual will prove to be usefull, but on
the whole, I don't think it will really change Tremere combat all that
much (as opposed to Thoughts Betrayed...), certainly not the point of
Shotgun Ritual being too good or a broken card (again, based on
assumptions...).

Assuming that Shotgun only allows the use of Strikes, and not Blood to
Water, the net result in most situations are either 1/2 Aggro (Walk of
Flame) for 3 Blood, 3/5 Damage (Cauldron) for 3 Blood, or 4/5 Blood
Stealing (Essence Drain) for 4 Blood (I am a bit iffy on some of the exact
numbers as I am working from memory. Please excuse any point glitches
:-). I can't think of any other important second round strikes off hand.
These are hardly out of line with other combat clans, especially
considering the cost (a Nosferatu/Brujah can punch for 7 for no Blood
cost...). Drain Essence seems to come off best out of all of them.

Mind you, I have no great love of the Tremere (I'm a hard working
Nosferatu, m'self), and I do somewhat subscribe to the Tremere Conspiracy
theories, but I don't think that Shotgun Ritual will really make all that
much of a difference in the long run, let alone make them too good (that
distinction is reserved for TB...).

>Obfuscate is getting an S:CE. IMHO, It should have had it from the
>beginning.
>
>Celerity is getting bleed; nice, but it's probably going to be really
>expensive and restricted(like cat burglary). If it's not, then I'll
>worry and complain with the rest of you.
>

>Thaumaturgy is getting first round aggs(gulp) via shotgun ritual. This
>_is_ a bad thing(TM). But not because it makes the clans alike; because
>it gives the tremere an ability which they, as far as I can tell, do not
>need, and have never needed.
>

>The cross over of disciplines is a good thing; it encourages diversity
>in deck construction, which adds to the game. I like the idea of some
>sick person out there making an effective Ventrue combat deck; maybe
>It'll become possible. Maybe not. But even the cross-over in Sabbat
>(With the exception of Ian Forestal) won't make it as mindless as you
>might think; some of the gangrel w/ dominate don't have protean at all.
>
>The ability to have a clan do something other than what it normally does

>adds an interesting aspect to the game; but without work and some skill
>in deck building, it will be difficult to make the clan as effective in
>the non-specialized area as in the specialized one. And such
divergences,
>in my experience, have been fragile and easily disrupted(My malkies w/
>flamethrowers deck is a good example; it dies when anyone pulls a
Rotshreck).
>That the possibility exists is good. Making it mindless(which I don't
think
>Sabbat will do; I can't see my Obfuscate/Protean/Dominate deck being too
easy
>to make even w/ Sabbat) is bad.
>

>Of course, if Sabbat does make it mindless I'll be just as ticked as you
are.
>But right now, I don't see that it will. We'll just have to wait
>and see the set to reach any conclusions.
>

>Alec Chang
>
>

Greetings to all,
As I'm still learning the ins-and-outs of quoting with this newsgroup
stuff I'll refrain from trying to do anything too daring.
Anyway I just wanted to say that I will wait to see what the new expansion
brings. I will, however, say that I don't want every discipline to have
their S:CE and their bleed enhancements and their damage
prevention/reduction and their agg damage and their stealth modifier and
intercept modifier just because it makes more things possible.
The disciplines should remain unique. They can explore some new areas,
even powerful areas, but they should not stray into powers normally in
other disciplines just to increase variety. Just my opinion.
Looking forward to seeing just how cool the Lasombra are,
Doug Dunaway

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
"Marc Erl" <er...@uni-muenster.de> writes:
>By the way - although I am on this Newsgroup for quite a while I cannot

>memorise all those abbreviations. What is S.CE???

Here's a list to get you going:

4CL: Four Card Limit - the usual CL (imported from MtG)
AoR: Army of Rats
B&B: Bruise and Bleed - put potential blockers in torpor and bleed freely
CCG: Collectible Card Game
CL: Card Limit (on the number of an individual card in the deck)
CTB: Cross Table Bleed - bleeding someone other than your prey
DBR: Dragon Breath Rounds
DCI: Duelist Convocation (official tournament makers)
DS: Dark Sovereigns - the first expansion to VtES
FoW: Force of Will (a DS card)
GT: Golden Tenets: no repeat actions and no vote pushing.
GtU: Govern the Unaligned
HG: Hunting Ground
IC: Inner Circle
KRC: Kine Resources Contested (also, a deck composed of mostly this card)
LSJ: L. Scott Johnson - keeper of lists :-)
Mask1K: Mask of a Thousand Faces
MOoT: Master: Out-of-Turn
MotB: Madness of the Bard (a DS card)
MotSB: Movement of the Slow Body (only found in Jyhad)
MS&B: Malkavian Stealth and Bleed (refers to the deck or the strategy)
MtG: Magic: the Gathering, the first successful CCG
MVH: Muddled Vampire Hunter
NC: Non-Camarilla
NCL: No card limits (same as NL)
NL: No Limits (on the number of an individual card in the deck)
OTP: One Trick Pony: a deck that does only one thing (usually degenerate)
P/J: Prince or Justicar
RoF: Reversal of Fortune (not to be confused with ROFL)
RTR: Rules Team Ruling - official interpretation of a card or rule
s/h/it: she/he/it (PCness taken to the Malkavian point of view)
S:CE: Strike: Combat Ends
S&B: Stealth and Bleed (or Sneak and Bleed, meaning the same thing)
SR: Sudden Reversal
TB: Thoughts Betrayed (a DS card)
TGFKAJ: The Game Formerly Know As Jyhad
TOM: Tom Wylie - WotC Net.Rep
VtES: Vampire: the Eternal Struggle (TGFKAJ)
WotC: Wizards of the Coast - makers of VtES and MtG
WwEF: Wake with Evening's Freshness
YASR: Yet Another Stupid Ruling

---

AFAIK: as far as I know
FWIW: for what it's worth
IIRC: if I recall correctly
IME: in my experience
IMHO: in my humble opinion
IMO: in my opinion
j/k: just kidding
LOL: laugh(ing) out loud (a lesser version of ROFL)
OTOH: on the other hand
ROFL: roll(ing) on (the) floor, laughing
ROFLMAO: ..., laughing mass off
TTBOMK: to the best of my knowledge
YMMV: your mileage may vary

I was discussing this with my brother the other day, and we
agreed that fortitude would be one of the more difficult disciplines to
create a S:CE card for. In the end, though, the concept we came up with
is basically "Walk Away". The vampire with fortitude simply walks away
from the combat. "Yeah, go ahead and shoot me in the back with DBR, I'll
just make my soak roll anyway." Yes, I know I used the RPG terms, but
V:TES uses disciplines at all levels, so I figure a high-enough level
fortitude would basically allow you to walk away from combat.

Messages.Author: DOUGDWISE
Messages.Body:
Greetings to all,
Just a quick question here. Why do you folks advocating a S:CE for every
discipline think it is necessary or desirable? Are combat decks that
destructive to your game environment?
I would imagine that a S:CE for every (or even most) disciplines would
just reduce the chances of anybody ever getting into combat without using
TB or IG or Psyche. And packing enough of these to allow a combat deck to
get to combat often enough to be effective in a S:CE rich evironment would
dilute the deck's damage dealing potential and make it less effective when
it does manage to have combat.
Since we haven't seen it yet, I assume the R&D folks at WotC haven't
decided to give each discipline a S:CE do it is kind of speculative at
this point. It remains one of the signature features of Presence and
Protean (any others? I can't recall offhand.)
Anyway, just to restate my question: why do the folks advocating giving
every discipline a S:CE think it is desirable or necessary?
Looking forward to hearing the response.

Doug Dunaway

Messages.Author: Nathan Harada
Messages.Body:
Doug, I really doubt anyone is advocating a S:CE for every
discipline. Right now, I think we're just trying to justify
the game-world terms for (maybe) giving Fortitude and Potence
a S:CE. I don't think it's a good thing, but it appears to
me that certain disciplines, such as Obfuscate, should have
had one in the basic set. (Maybe this is just me.)
Put this way-I don't think that any of the combat
disciplines-Fortitude, Potence, Thaumaturgy (Celerity has
Riposte) should get S:CEs. Auspex and Dominate really
should not have anything to S:CE. Dominate has Obedience,
Auspex Read Intentions. Animalism? What?
Although an S:CE could be justified in each of these
cases, it should not. As long as the S:CEs are limited, I
don't have a problem. Justification for things later doesn't
make them a good thing for the game.

-Nathan Harada

Messages.Author: Daniel H. Levine
Messages.Body:
First of all, somewhat in WoTC's defence: the Ventrue *antitribu* of
the Sabbat have Auspex rather than Presence as a clan (bloodline,
technically) discipline in the tabletop game.
This raises a question I'd like to hear people's opinions on, though.
There are certain combinations of disciplines that seem to be
extremely (some would argue: too) effective. Case in point being the
Malkavian's Dominate+Obfuscate. Now, (presumably) the reason behind
certain clans having certain combos is that those are the disciplines
from the RPG.
What to people think would be the best way to fix this (in theory, not
like anyone from WoTC would pay attention to a discussion like this
:)? Would it be worthwhile to fix it (some people obviously think
that it would)? Would it be better to change the clan's discipline
mixes in the card game, moving away from the RPG, or would a
preferable fix be to have designed the card effects with an eye toward
the combinations available, even at the expense of card effects that
were counterintuitive to the disciplines' presumed effects (like, say,
if Dominate had been a combat discipline)?

Daniel Levine

Messages.Author: Canticle
Messages.Body:
: pel...@odyssee.net (Daniel H. Levine) wrote in article

: This raises a question I'd like to hear people's opinions on, though.

: There are certain combinations of disciplines that seem to be
: extremely (some would argue: too) effective. Case in point being the
: Malkavian's Dominate+Obfuscate. Now, (presumably) the reason behind

: from the RPG.

More than likely...personally, I picked up the game only because I really
enjoy playing the RPG...and used to enjoy to the LARP. It would be hard
for the CCG to remain close to the RPG if they started mixing and matching
disciplines on a whim.

I won't argue Malkavian Obfuscate+Dominate though...in the LARP I was in,
my character was the Malkavian Primogen. Dominate+Obfuscate+a tiny bit of
Thaumaturgy made a lot of lives hell. It makes life hell in the card game
as well.

Personally, I think the biggest mistake WotC made was creating cards
dependent on Rock-Paper-Scissors...my reputation from the LARP has
followed me into the card game, and no one allows me to play Rock Paper
Scissors at all...I always seem to win or tie.

: What to people think would be the best way to fix this (in theory, not

: like anyone from WoTC would pay attention to a discussion like this

: :)? Would it be worthwhile to fix it (some people obviously think

: that it would)? Would it be better to change the clan's discipline
: mixes in the card game, moving away from the RPG, or would a
: preferable fix be to have designed the card effects with an eye toward
: the combinations available, even at the expense of card effects that
: were counterintuitive to the disciplines' presumed effects (like, say,
: if Dominate had been a combat discipline)?

I think, personally, that they perhaps should have tried to balance out
the disciplines a little more, although given the nature of card game
mechanics and the complexity of V:TES, it's a task I wouldn't envy.

Moving away from the RPG would probably turn away a lot of people who play
the game (myself, for one). I picked it up because it was a cool way to
get into the Vampire politics aspect of the Vampire:RPG without having to
sit down with a bunch of people whose characters act more like Imperial
Marines from Warhammer. The LARP wasn't much better...so far, the CCG
satisfies my scheming political brain just fine. Moving away from the RPG
wouldn't impress me, or some of the people I play with.
